To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The matrix element of the spin of a gluon in a nucleon is not a gauge-invariant quantity; (2) The matrix element in a particular gauge can be transformed to another gauge using a simple formula; (3) The same formula can be used to obtain the matrix element for other manifestly-gauge-dependent operators present in QCD.
the matrix element of a gluon spin operator is not invariant under an arbitrary gauge transformation.

the spin of the gluon does not contribute in a gauge invariant way to the nucleon spin, and that the matrix element of a gluon spin operator can be obtained in a different gauge from a calculation in any gauge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the spin and orbital angular momentum of the quarks in the nucleon, as measured by the quark spin and orbital angular momenta operators.
the study of the gluon helicity in the nucleon.
the study of the spin of the nucleon.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the matrix element of any gauge-dependent operator in the nucleon helicity basis is not gauge-invariant.
the matrix element of any operator that is not gauge invariant cannot be determined from a calculation performed in a specific gauge.
the matrix element of gluon spin is not invariant under general gauge transformations, and that the gluon spin does not contribute in a gauge invariant way to nucleon helicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a way to make the gluon spin contribution to nucleon spin manifestly gauge invariant, and we have found the gauge-invariant form of the gluon angular momentum operator.
the matrix elements of the gluon angular momentum operator are gauge dependent.
the gluon spin contribution in the proton spin is gauge-dependent and the matrix element of any operator in the QCD spin sum is gauge-dependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gluon spin contribution to nucleon spin is gauge dependent, but the gauge dependence is not arbitrary.

the matrix element of a manifestly gauge-dependent operator in a nucleon helicity state can be obtained from a calculation made for that operator in a different gauge by a simple change of basis in the space of operators.
the gluon spin contribution to the nucleon spin is not gauge invariant, and therefore cannot be calculated in a gauge-invariance-preserving way in QCD.
